As others have stated, be sure to keep your hardware (mounting bracket, bail arm, wire harness). Installed in minutes. On my particular freezer, I needed to replace the bail arm that came with this one with the one on my old icemaker as this one was too short to trigger when the door was opened or when the ice tray became full.

One thing to note, I was expecting this to work immediately (fill tray with water, etc.). When it did not, I called the local repair shop assuming there was another issue. However, after a few hours, it filled with water and started producing ice. I assume this was because the ice maker need time to cool to freezer temp before filling to make ice. So far no issues.

As others have stated, this is a bare bones ice maker replacement. No wiring harness. No clips. I transferred my double wire hanger from my original Amana ice maker to this one, to ensure ice maker shuts off when the bin is full. The single wire hanger doesn't raise high enough as the ice bin fills to activate the shut-off mechanism. I added a picture of the double wire hanger.
The piece for the water fill tube indicates the area where a "tab" should be removed to allow for the tube, but that tab doesn't just snap out, though it looks like it should. You have to cut it out with a knife, or some other tool (I used a Dremel), though it probably would have been easier to use the original piece from my old unit.
You may need to "prime" the ice maker after installation. This can be done by removing the front white cover and inserting a small INSULATED jumper cable into the holes identified with "T" and "H". You can find instructions on how to do this safely on YouTube (Search "Testing Ice Maker").
I kept most of the items from my old unit in case anything fails or breaks on this new one in the future, such as the thermostat, sweeper arms, and tray (for the heater element).
I just installed this and it is working properly. If something changes, or it fails in a short time, I will adjust my star rating and update my review.

I have pet chickens -very enthusiastic chickens - and found myself with an overabundance of eggs when they started laying this summer.  I needed a storage solution - one that I could safely stack in the fridge. I purchased one of these trays, tried it out and have ordered more.  They are easily hand washed (not dishwasher safe). They stack nicely to easily store a lot of eggs. The only drawback is that they are hard plastic and I was concerned about dropping eggs into place and cracking them. My solution? Padding placed in the bottom of each egg compartment: a small folded square cut from a paper towel. It's just enough padding and works perfectly. One last hint: put the eggs in with the larger end up - this makes them easier to remove.
